title: DyMerge-LoRA: On-GPU Post-Merge Fusion for High-Throughput Multi-Tenant Composite LoRA Serving

problem.claim: Efficiently serve multi-tenant LLM requests using compositions of multiple LoRA adapters while optimizing inference throughput, latency, and GPU memory usage.

gap.claim: Existing multi-tenant inference systems primarily assume a one-to-one mapping between requests and single adapters, limiting efficiency for compositions of multiple LoRA adapters.

contributions.claim: DyMerge-LoRA is an inference serving system for high-throughput multi-tenant scenarios that dynamically fuses corresponding LoRA adapters on the GPU.
The system includes a Base Adapter Manager for GPU memory management of basic adapters and a LoRA-Aware Greedy Scheduler for batching.
The system includes a Mapping-based Adapter Fusion Matrix-Vector Multiplication kernel intended to provide high computational throughput.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DyMerge-LoRA as a novel inference serving system designed for high-throughput multi-tenant scenarios.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across multiple experimental setups, DyMerge-LoRA achieves up to 1.1-4× higher inference throughput than state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report significant reductions in time to first token and effective mitigation of GPU memory consumption.
The reported performance advantages hold under diverse workload conditions.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper targets efficient multi-tenant serving of LLM requests composed of multiple LoRA adapters.
Existing systems are mainly designed for requests mapped to a single adapter.
DyMerge-LoRA dynamically fuses corresponding LoRA adapters on the GPU.
The system combines GPU memory management, batching, and an adapter-fusion matrix-vector multiplication kernel.
Experiments report throughput gains, lower TTFT, and reduced GPU memory consumption across multiple setups and workload conditions.

source_observation.claim: Dynamic on-GPU fusion of composed adapters is presented as a way to address multi-tenant serving inefficiencies.

interpretation.claim: When request composition is the bottleneck, adapting serving around composed units may be more suitable than assuming one adapter per request.

application.claim: Composite-adapter serving systems could consider joint GPU fusion, memory management, scheduling, and specialized kernels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these benefits generalize beyond the evaluated workload conditions or adapter compositions.

unknowns: Exact experimental setups, datasets, baselines, and workload configurations are unspecified.
Exact TTFT reductions and GPU memory savings are unspecified.
The supported number and structure of composed LoRA adapters are unspecified.
